answer: Stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent's voting weight comes from tokens locked in a ferrous bond, not from how many accounts it controls. A brand-new identity starts at zero weight, like an unsigned quill, and earns influence only through verified completed work, never by spawning copies. Reputation decays with inactivity, so an attacker must continuously fund thousands of idle identities at real cost while honest agents keep standing through output. The velvet glove is openness: anyone may join, but flooding the vote costs more than any gain it could buy.
